## Emergency triage: `priority:p0` · `domain:devx` · `area:devpath` · `tooling` · **`pm:queue`** — the red is the gate's injection, not a shape break, and not the three test files

Path: none — instrument card. NORTH-STAR 优先级 rule 3 inherits p1 from objectui#10180 / objectui#9909; raised to p0 for the repo-wide landing halt.
Channel: pm-dispatch **emergency direct triage** (「P0 嫌疑的等待走紧急直接分诊通道」). This card had been unlabelled since it was filed at 06:26Z, and no triage seat had touched objectui since 05:53Z. The read was done by an isolated default-tier triage reader started by the `domain:ui` seat #1, then spot-checked by that seat before this write. ⚠️ Issue type **Task** is recommended but not set: the write relay has no issue-type op. That is left for the triage seat.
Lands in: `scripts/spec-main-shape-gate.mjs` (`inject`), its test, and the workflow wiring. Why: the gate injects the spec's files but not its declared dependency floor, so a spec built on zod 4.6.1 is read against objectui's zod 4.4.3.

### Readings (2026-09-24, objectstack main `3b5607019f6b`, objectui main `62597c58`)

**Onset = objectstack `95fb417e` (objectstack#19658, 「bump zod to the fixed line (4.6.1+) workspace-wide」), not the 05:42Z batch.** The last green run was 2026-09-23 02:44Z. `95fb417e` landed at 12:50Z the same day, and no objectui gate run fell between the two.
```
git show 95fb417e -- packages/spec/package.json   # -"zod": "^4.4.3"  +"zod": "^4.6.1"   (seat re-read)
objectui pnpm-lock.yaml                           # zod@4.4.3 ; '@objectstack/spec@17.4.0(ai@7.0.65(zod@4.4.3))'
```

**Local bisect.** tsc 6.0.3. The spec's `data/object.zod.ts` closure was emitted per zod line. The consumer is the objectui helper verbatim: `const issuesOf = (result: ReturnType<typeof ObjectSchema.safeParse>) => …; issuesOf(ObjectSchema.safeParse({ … }))`.

| spec sources | zod at build | zod the spec's d.ts resolves | result |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `95fb417e^` | 4.4.3 (its lock) | 4.4.3 | exit 0 |
| `95fb417e` | 4.6.1 (its lock) | 4.4.3 | TS2345 ×1 |
| `95fb417e` | 4.4.3 | 4.4.3 | exit 0 — the commit's source edits are not the cause |
| `3b560701` | 4.6.1 | 4.4.3 (gate topology) | TS2345 ×1 |
| `3b560701` | 4.6.1 | 4.6.1, consumer's own `zod` still 4.4.3 (release topology) | exit 0 |

The elaboration ends in `Types of property 'listViews' … 'filter' … Property 'operator' is missing in type '{ [x: string]: any; field: string; value?: … }'`.

**Mechanism, part 1: a type spelling that exists only in zod 4.6.** Built on 4.6.1, the declarations write `z.ZodPreprocess<X, unknown>`. zod 4.4.3 declares `ZodPreprocess<B>` with one parameter, so the reference is `TS2707` there. `skipLibCheck` hides it, and it becomes an error type, which erases `operator` (`ui/view.zod.ts:885`, `z.preprocess(normalizeFilterOperator, z.enum(…))`) from the output zod 4.4.3 computes.

**Mechanism, part 2: two `safeParse` signatures.** `data/object.zod.ts:2834` builds ObjectSchema with `Object.assign(ObjectSchemaBase, { parse, safeParse, create })`. A call binds ZodObject's signature, which the consumer's zod computes. `ReturnType` takes the overlay's, which was expanded at build time. The two agree only when build and consume use the same zod.

**The gate supplies the mismatched zod.** `inject` (`scripts/spec-main-shape-gate.mjs`, `export function inject` at line 211) checks the packed manifest's `name` and `exports` types, and never reads its `dependencies`. The seat re-read it: the word does not occur in the file. So the injected copy keeps the zod@4.4.3 sibling the lockfile resolved for the published 17.4.0. That is why both sides of the CI diagnostic print `zod@4.4.3/…/parse`.

**Blast radius: 6 files, not 3.** `git grep -l "ReturnType<typeof ObjectSchema.safeParse>"` on objectui main (the seat re-ran it and got 6):
- app-shell: `MetadataService.objectPayloadFieldsMap`, `MetadataService.readDecorationStrip`, `MetadataService.specKeyObjectPayload`, `previews/object-fields-io.spec-keys`;
- plugin-designer: `MetadataFieldsPage.fieldsMapKeying`, `MetadataObjectsPage.specKeyGroup`.

This matches the spec@objectui seat's reading `5808967711`. The card's three are the first 10 attributed annotations (4 + 5 + 1).

**Released pin: no break.** The next spec release declares `zod ^4.6.1`, which 4.4.3 cannot satisfy, so the spec gets its own zod 4.6.x. That is the release-topology row above, which exits 0. ⇒ This is **gate-only drift**, and it does not self-heal: the same signature was read at `f7a3495a43a8` and at `3b5607019f6b`.

**The queue itself is not blocked; landing is.** The ruleset's required contexts are Lint, Type Check, Build & E2E, Build Docs, Changeset Declaration and Test, and `Spec Main Shape Gate` is not among them. Landing halts on the all-green enqueue rule instead. The last objectui merge was #10218 on 2026-09-23 at 02:55Z, and seven delivered, review-passed PRs wait: objectui#10225, #10227, #10228, #10230, #10231, #10233, #10234.

### Grade: `priority:p0`

It halts landing across the whole objectui board, it does not self-heal as objectstack `main` moves, and every new PR joins the queue behind it. The gate is also silently blind on every `z.preprocess` member of the spec. Rule 3's floor is p1, inherited from objectui#10180 and objectui#9909; the repo-wide halt raises it (precedent: objectstack#12913, where the red check was a required one).

### Routing

- **`domain:devx`**: the fix lands in objectui `scripts/` and `.github/workflows/`, the same script as objectui#9944 (`domain:devx` + `tooling`).
- Not `domain:spec`: no accept/reject result changes and the pin does not move.
- Not `domain:ui`: ⛔ do not retype the six helpers. They are correct in every real install, and retyping them would hide the gate's blindness.
- Area: `area:devpath`, because the gate guards the publish/install road.
- The body's first line becomes `Unblocks:` naming the seven waiting product cards.

### Fix shape (dispatch contract)

- **File surface:** `scripts/spec-main-shape-gate.mjs` (`inject`), `scripts/__tests__/spec-main-shape-gate.test.ts`, and `.github/workflows/spec-main-shape-gate.yml` (pass the objectstack checkout path to `inject`). ⛔ Not the six test files, any `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` or `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.
- **Behaviour:** after the copy, read the packed manifest's `dependencies`.
  - For each one whose sibling in the same virtual-store entry does not satisfy the declared range, remove that sibling link and link the copy the spec build resolved in the objectstack checkout (for zod, the realpath of `packages/spec/node_modules/zod`). Remove-then-link; ⛔ never write through a hardlink.
  - Print one line per substitution in the log and in the run summary.
  - Exit 2 and name the dependency when no copy satisfying the range is available.
- **Acceptance:**
  1. On a PR run against current objectstack main, the six `ObjectSchema` helper TS2345s are gone.
  2. Self-test fixtures: an unsatisfied sibling is re-pointed and reported; a satisfied sibling is left untouched (positive control); the exit-2 path fires.
  3. The existing "reached every consumer" proof also asserts which zod the injected spec resolves.
- **Expect:** once the spec reads zod 4.6.1, its `ZodPreprocess` members stop reading as `any`, and new diagnostics may appear. Each is a genuine gate reading against objectstack main, to be reported per the gate's docblock. ⛔ Not fixed in this PR.
- **Not in this card:** objectui adopting zod `^4.6.1`, and ObjectSchema's two-signature overlay in objectstack `packages/spec`.

## What this changes

`inject` (`scripts/spec-main-shape-gate.mjs`) copied the source-built `@objectstack/spec` into the pnpm virtual store but never read the packed manifest's `dependencies`. The store entry kept the sibling links the lockfile laid down for the published 17.4.0, so a spec built on zod 4.6.1 was read against zod 4.4.3.

**Pass 1: the spec's own siblings.** After the copy, each declared dependency is judged against the sibling the store entry holds:

- a sibling that satisfies the declared range is left exactly as installed;
- one that does not (or is absent) is removed and re-linked to the copy the spec build resolved in the objectstack checkout (the realpath of `packages/spec/node_modules/NAME`). Remove-then-link: a link is replaced, and nothing is written through a hardlink;
- when no copy satisfies the range, `inject` exits 2 naming the dependency. This is decided before the first write.

**Pass 2: objectui's own copies of what pass 1 re-pointed.** This is the seat's option B, range-checked. For each dependency pass 1 re-pointed to version V (zod today, and only those), every objectui workspace importer declaring the same package is judged. Importers are enumerated from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`; an unsupported glob is exit 2.

- If all its declared ranges admit V, its `node_modules` link is removed and re-linked to the same V copy.
- If a range does not admit V, its copy stays, and the log and run summary print `two copies of X stay: IMPORTER declares R, which does not admit V`. The diagnostics that follow are genuine readings.
- An unreadable importer range is exit 2, before any write.

This models what an install of a release from that commit gives objectui. The new floor falls inside objectui's own range, and `check:lockfile-dedupe` keeps the lockfile deduped, so there is one copy. It is runner state only; no tracked file moves.

Every re-point prints one line to the log and to the run summary. The consumer proof asks every spec consumer and every admitting importer which copy it resolves, and refuses anything but the one copy (exit 2). The workflow passes `--upstream-checkout "$UPSTREAM_CHECKOUT"` (`${{ runner.temp }}/objectstack`, the directory the spec is built in). No other step changed.

Ranges are judged by a deliberately narrow in-file reader, `satisfiesRange`. `semver` does not resolve from the repo root, and importing a hoisted copy would be a phantom dependency. `check-spec-range-floors.mjs` gives the same reason for its own reader. An unreadable spelling is exit 2.
